_about: One registry of the spots: where each spot is, which vertical datum its sea-floor map uses, and the Stage A grid.
Read by live-data/spots.py, live-data/build_snapshot.py, pieces/06-live-wave/sites.py and stage_a.py,
Change a value here and every Python script picks it up. The browser viewer keeps its own copy
(pieces/01-seafloor/viewer/live_core.js LIVE_SPOTS and others): change those by hand until it reads this file.
Fields: name = short name (live panel); title = long name (renders, case files);
lat/lon = the point the live forecast cells are picked around (decimal degrees, lon negative west);
datum = vertical datum of the spot's sea-floor map (null: no map with a swell model);
msl_to_datum_m = added to a forecast sea level (MSL) to get the tide above that datum (Peniche: LAT = MSL - 1.66 m);
takeoff = the surf spot's take-off point and where the coordinate comes from;
viewer_points = the spot's point-cloud file in pieces/01-seafloor/viewer/data/;
typical_swell = the 'typical winter swell' the illustrative runs use (H0 m, T s, direction FROM deg, tide m above datum);
stage_a = the Stage A reef-model grid (pieces/06-live-wave/sites.py explains each field).

takeoff.how: published spot position (Wikipedia, Banzai Pipeline), approximate
model break onset nearest the cited Supertubos coordinate (39.34, -9.36, which is on land); approximate
published La Graviere position (surf-guide source), approximate
